Milindapraśna
or °pañhā(ho). Bud. Pāli. dialogue between Milinda, King of Sāgala an. the Buddhist monk Nāgasena expostulating the texts of Buddhism (2nd cent. B. C.).
See Wint, HIL. Vol. II. p.. 168-177; also Encycl. Dict of Pāli Lit. p.. 323-30; also Āyurved kā Bṛhat Itihās, p.. 139-45.
On its historicity, see L. A. Waddel, A Historical basis for the questions of King ‘Menander’ from the Tibetan etc., JRAS (1897) 227-37.
Br. Mus. Pāli p. 142. Cambr. 85. Cambr. Uni. Pāli p. 146. Colombo p. 51 (2 mss.). Colombo D. I. 1154. 1803. Copen. Pāli p. 148 (2 mss.). Fausboll 126-27. IO. Pāli p. 119 (no. 96) (no. 97). Leumann 74. Paris Pāli p. 35 (2 mss.).
mentioned in a. inscription a. Pagan dated 1442 A. D. Ref. “Pāli tracts in inscriptions'’ in the J. Myth. Soc. XXII. p. 413. [Page225-b]
Pt.. (1) ed. by V. Trenckner, London, 1880. (2) Harward Oriental Ser. Vol. III. in parts. Harvard University, Leipzig, 1891. (3) ed. in Siamese script, Bangkok, 1925. C.. J.. 209 (1926) 179. (4) Rahul Prakashan, Delhi, 2000.
See Br. Mus. Pt.. Bk.. 1876-92. 234; 1892-1906. 8. 386. 853.
Transls.:
English: by T. W. Rhys Davids, SBE. Vol.. 35. 36.
French: Le Questions de Milinda, Milindapanha, by Louis Finot, Paris, 1923.
German: in parts. by F. O. Schrader, Berlin, 1905; by Bhikkhu Nyanatiloka, Munchen, 1919.
Hindi: ed. an. transl. by Swami Dwarikadasasastri, Baudh. Bharati Ser. 13, Benares, 1990 (2nd edn.).
For the Chinese transl. of the names in the work, see Paul Pelliot, Les noms propres dans les traductions chinoises du Milindapañha, J. Ser. H. Vol. IV (Jul. dec. 1914) 379-419.
On its extra Indian transl.., see J. Takakusu, Chinese translations of the Milinda Pañha, JRAS (1896) 1-21. |20|225

Milindarāja
king of Ratanpura in Ceylon; disciple of Medhaṅkara Mahāthera of Sovaṇṇamaya Mahāvihāra (a. of Loka(pp.)dīpa(ka)sāra, Fausboll 134). See Wint. HIL. II. p. 214. fn. 3. |20|226

Milhaṇa
son of Kuloddhāra.
--Cikitsāmṛta. med. composed in 1224 A. D. See under the text.
